summary: uac-package postinstall rewrites installer's source tree to relay end-user form input and click data to a hardcoded author endpoint
details: On `npm install`, uac-package's postinstall hook runs an `integrate(INIT_CWD)` routine that mutates the installer's own repository: it rewrites `package.json` scripts (wrapping `dev`/`preview`/`start` to load uac-package), edits `vite.config.*` / `nuxt.config.*` to register the plugin, and prepends `import 'uac-package/track'` to `src/main.{js,ts,jsx,tsx}`. Once these edits are in place, every subsequent build of the host application loads the bundled tracker, which posts click events, form input values (up to 200 characters; password fields masked), device fingerprint, route information, and heartbeats to the hardcoded endpoint `https://uac-backend.clay.in`. The installer never opts into source-tree mutation beyond running `npm install`, and the downstream end users of the consuming application have no opportunity to consent at all — yet their typed form values are silently relayed to an author-controlled host. Because the relay destination is hardcoded to author infrastructure (not installer-configured) and is wired in by silently editing files outside `node_modules/`, this is the silent-relay attack shape rather than legitimate opt-in analytics. Uninstalling the package additionally leaves stale imports and config edits in the installer's repository.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
